hero.title: Biotechnology in Mauritius
hero.subtitle: **Biotechnology in Mauritius for Indian Students** is a study pathway for students who are interested in genetics, microbiology, molecular biology, pharmaceutical research, food technology and industrial innovation. It merges biology with laboratory techniques and technology, creating applications in healthcare, agriculture, food production and environmental protection. Students who want to **Study Biotechnology in Mauritius** can explore different undergraduate and diploma-level options.

overview: The University of Mauritius offers a BSc (Hons) Pharmaceutical Biotechnology listed for the 2026–2027 academic year, while the University of Technology, Mauritius, lists a Diploma in Industrial Biotechnology. These provide starting points for students exploring biotechnology education in the country. **Edu-Hawk Worldwide** recommends checking the current programme availability and admission requirements before applying.

faq.question: Can Indian students study biotechnology in Mauritius?
faq.answer: Indian students can explore biotechnology-related programmes, subject to the institution's international admission requirements, academic eligibility and intake availability. Edu-Hawk Worldwide can help students understand the admission considerations for Biotechnology in Mauritius for Indian Students.

faq.question: How long does it take to study biotechnology in Mauritius?
faq.answer: The University of Mauritius lists its BSc (Hons) Pharmaceutical Biotechnology as a 3.5-year full-time programme. The University of Technology, Mauritius, lists its Diploma in Industrial Biotechnology as two years full-time or three years part-time.

faq.question: What is the cost of studying biotechnology in Mauritius?
faq.answer: Fees vary by programme and student category. Obtain a current international-student fee schedule from the institution, including tuition, registration, laboratory expenses and other compulsory costs.

faq.question: What are the career options after biotechnology?
faq.answer: Graduates may explore pharmaceutical production, laboratory testing, food technology, agricultural biotechnology, environmental testing and research support. Advanced research and specialised positions may require postgraduate qualifications.

faq.question: Is a biotechnology degree from Mauritius recognised in India?
faq.answer: Recognition depends on the institution, awarding body, programme and the requirements applicable to the intended job or further study. Before enrolling, verify the qualification with the relevant Indian university, employer or regulatory authority, particularly if the course is a specialised professional programme.
